2: A prayer of one afflicted, when he grows faint and pours out his lament before Yahweh. O Yahweh, hear my prayer, and let my cry for help come to you.
3: Do not hide your face from me in the day of my trouble. Incline your ear to me. In the day I call, answer me quickly,
4: for my days vanish in smoke, and my bones are charred like a hearth.
5: My heart is struck like grass and withers. Indeed, I forget to eat my bread.
6: Because of the sound of my groaning my bones cling to my skin.
7: I am like an owl of the wilderness; I am like a little owl of the ruins.
8: I lie awake and I am like a lone bird on a roof.
9: All the day my enemies reproach me; those who mock me swear oaths against me.
10: Indeed, I eat ashes like bread and mix my drink with tears
11: because of your indignation and anger, for you have picked me up and thrown me away.
12: My days are like a lengthened shadow, and I wither like grass.
13: But you, O Yahweh, abide forever, and your remembrance ⌞from generation to generation⌟.
14: You rise up and take pity on Zion, because it is time to favor it, for the appointed time has come.
15: Your servants take pleasure in her stones, and show favor to its dust.
16: Then the nations will fear the name of Yahweh, and all the kings of the earth your glory.
17: For Yahweh will rebuild Zion; he will appear in his glory.
18: He will turn his attention to the prayer of the destitute and will not despise their prayer.
19: Let this be written for the next generation, so that a people yet to be created may praise Yah,
20: that he looked down from his holy height. Yahweh looked from heaven over the earth
21: to hear the groaning of the prisoner, to liberate ⌞those destined to die⌟,
22: so that they may make known in Zion the name of Yahweh, and his praise in Jerusalem,
23: when the peoples assemble, together with kingdoms, to serve Yahweh.
24: He has broken my strength along the way; he has cut short my days.
25: I say, “My God, do not carry me off from my life in the middle of my days.” Your years continue throughout all generations.
26: Long ago you laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
27: They will perish, but you will endure. And like a garment they will all wear out, you will replace them like clothing, and they will be set aside.
28: But you are the same, and your years do not end.
29: The children of your servants will continue, and their ⌞descendants⌟ will be established before you.
